host: benjamin, macOS ARM64, Tailscale SSH Background launchd session
method: Two unique temporary one-shot Background launchd jobs ran a test-only Python parent that forked a bounded eight-second child. The parent exited normally after the child recorded its identity. One child remained in its parent's process group; the other called setsid first. A separate ps observation was taken one second after the parent marker. No workload process was signaled. After waiting for natural expiry, each exact task label was unloaded and absence checked. A later read-only SSH check found neither observed PID nor the task directory.
cleanup: Both exact job labels absent, task-owned temporary directory removed; a later ps check did not find either recorded PID.
scope: Single-host Background-session observation, test-only Python; not an Amu workload, actual bot, inference process, lock test, or production qualification. The one-second ps samples do not prove timing for all process trees. launchd job disappearance is insufficient evidence that an escaped descendant has ended. This extends the prior local GUI-session lock/setsid observation to the remote Background session, but does not qualify a process-lifetime boundary or governor.
